Lost in Transition - Identity in a changing world
It's Monday, what have you done to prepare?

Lost a bit more weight and got a bit more fit.

Round one of seedlings for indoor/outdoor gardens doing well, so starting round two later today. Added to and rotated the existing water reserves.

Did my monthly "dump the bag, evaluate the contents, repack" on all my bags (EDC, Get Home, Bugout, Get Out of Dodge, etc.).

Practiced my knot-making skills. Checked and sharpened most of the knives. Cleaned and rechecked the alignment of all the security cameras. Reviewed the recordings for suspicious activity.
What were your thoughts when you checked your bags?

This is going to be long, but basically:

Is this item still essential? What does it do? How well does it do it? Can I replace it with something lighter/more functional/more durable?

If a medical item, is it expired (or will it expire before my next scheduled check)? Has it been exposed to conditions which might have compromised its effectiveness (heat/cold from trunk, excessive moisture)? Have I used items that must be replenished (bandages, wipes, quick-clot, meds)? It it still appropriate for the season/conditions (mosquito spray in winter? Hand warmers in summer?)?

How long have ranger rolled clothes been packed? Are they appropriate for the season/expected weather?

For items in bags that get used often (knives, electronics, reserve battery packs, etc.): Are they still sharp/functioning properly/charged? Enough ammo left? Enough of those energy bars still there? Enough paracord still on the roll? Duct tape? Lenses on optics clean?

And, of course: Is the bag, taken as a whole, still going to do the job I need it to do? Are the items packed in a way so I can get to what I need for the situation its designed for? Can I (still) carry the damn thing? If I had to leave it behind or it became compromised, what are my options?
And was your pack up to par? Did you have to change anything?

My packs are always "up to par," but that doesn't mean they can't always be improved upon. So, yes, I always end up changing something.

One misconception I've noted among the prepping community is that a pack somehow "goes into stasis" once you load it up. It's there, always ready, and never has to change. That's false. Seasons change. Weather changes. Life changes. YOU change. Your pack must, therefore, also change and adapt over time.

For example, I just removed a spare hand warmer in my EDC pack. Around here, Winter is taking an early vacation and I don't anticipate needing it. Packed an extra energy bar and some chocolate covered coffee beans in its place.

It was time to swap out some of the ranger rolled winter gear for some warmer ones. If winter makes a return, they'll get exchanged again on the next bag check.
